subject: dragonling
reasoning:
I'm planning out a compact baby dragon model using the SDK—about 0.6m tall, chubby with a big head, small wings, tail, horns, and four legs, standing in a rest pose with legs apart and wings extended.

Working out the skeleton now: hips as the root joint, with a spine chain running forward into the chest and neck, and a tail chain running backward, both parented off the hips. I'm sweeping the body geometry along a catmull curve from the tail tip through the hips to the chest to keep the silhouette smooth and anatomically coherent.

Totaling the path segments gives rootT around 0.70, so I'm spacing six radius keys evenly across the body profile from tail tip to chest, roughly 0.012 up to 0.16, keeping the belly chubby near t=0.8. I'm checking that the body's bottom edge sits around y=0.18 so the legs, about 0.3 long, can reach down to feet near y=0.03.

For coloring I'll apply a simple countershade paint, green on the back fading to cream on the belly, applied mainly to the body sweep, neck, and head rather than every segment. The neck will be built as a short catmull-rom chain running from the chest joint up to the head base, parented to the last spine joint.

Now I'm defining the head joint positioned at the end of the neck chain, parented to the final neck joint, and attaching a scaled skull sphere offset slightly forward and up from it.

Still shaping the snout and jaw geometry...

Now working out nostrils as small spheres on the snout, and the eyes as amber spheres with dark pupils placed symmetrically using a side multiplier for left/right positioning. I'm double-checking that the eye placement sits just outside the skull sphere's radius so it reads correctly, then offsetting the pupils slightly further forward and outward.

Adding a tiny white highlight to each eye and making sure the head bone is explicitly set for proper attachment, then starting the horns as curved sweeps using bezier control points anchored to the head for a swept-back shape.

Still sculpting horns and spikes...

Using a bell-curve sizing based on t for the spikes, with small dorsal spikes along the neck too. Now I'm positioning the four legs—front legs from chest to shoulder and foot points, and hind legs with hip and foot coordinates, working out the digitigrade bend lengths and distances.

Naming each limb segment per side (shoulder/elbow/wrist for front, hip/knee/ankle for hind) so the chain joints map cleanly, with the limb points forming a polyline that the chain system follows and aims its tip along the end tangent, then parenting the front chain to the appropriate shoulder joint.

I'm working out which spine joint each leg chain attaches to—front legs off the upper spine joint, hind legs off the core/hips—and setting left/right sides based on x position. Then I'm sweeping each leg as a tapered tube (thicker for the hind thighs), and building a simple three-toed foot with small spikes radiating from the tip joint.

Now I'm placing the foot as a flattened ellipsoid bound to the leg's tip bone, making sure its bottom rests right at ground level, then adding forward-pointing claw spikes for the toes.

I'm assigning paint colors so legs stay plain green while the belly gets the cream tone, and I'm starting to sketch small wings attached at the shoulders along the back.

Working out the wing joint chain from shoulder to elbow to wrist, then branching out finger spans from the wrist as short two-point paths.

Still placing wing joints...

For that last membrane I'll default the edge B bone to the front joint and let the rest follow defaults. The membranes should be soft orange-pink, double-sided with thickness, and the wings should lean slightly back given the wrist and tip positioning. Finally, I'll shape the tail tip into a flame or spade by extruding that shape at the tail's end.

I'm reworking the tail's curve to lift it upward near the tip rather than drooping down, adjusting the body path points so the tail arcs up from the base, stays above the floor with enough radius at its lowest point, and tapers properly toward the tip.

That radius checks out fine. Now for the tail-tip spade, I'm working out the orientation vectors so the extruded outline lies flat in the horizontal plane, pointing backward along the tail rather than standing vertically.

Defining the spade's outline points...

Now I'm working out the bone chain for the tail, making sure the joints run root to tip for the extrude, then thinking about how to add belly plate stripes.

I'm skipping cheek blush and adding small dark nostril spheres positioned on top of the snout using the head bone's local coordinates, checking that the placement stays within the snout box bounds.

Now I'm placing downward-pointing cone teeth on the upper jaw using head-local positioning, and setting up the jaw bone joint with its pivot and aim points for the lower jaw.

For the lower jaw box, I'm computing box corners in head-local space, checking that the chin stays within the skull sphere's surface, and confirming local directions map correctly to model-forward orientation. I'll skip the tongue for now, set the lower jaw to a cream belly color, and add small brow ridge capsules above the eyes.

Now I'm placing cheek frill spikes at the sides using head-local coordinates, adjusting the "back" direction to a negative forward value, and defining the neck chain sweep path with front-to-back points and tapering radius for the paint-coat colored neck.

I'm checking joint placement: the head center sits forward and up from the neck joint, with horn bases and tips extending above the head radius. For the neck chain, I'm working out that a 3-point catmull spline gives 2 spans, so I'll name the joints "neck1" and "neck2" and parent the sweep to the last front joint.

I'm confirming the chain hierarchy — hind legs attach to the core, front legs to the front chain, spine and tail chains get their own named joints — then setting up the body sweep using the back, core, and front paths together with the coat color, and planning spikes positioned along that sweep.

Now I'm adding haunch and shoulder blobs as chubby sphere shapes at the hip and shoulder joints to give the legs some bulk, tying each to its corresponding bone before defining the actual limb points.

For the legs themselves I'm computing root and target positions for front and hind legs, picking bend directions so elbows bend back and knees bend forward, checking the distances against segment lengths to make sure they're plausible, then building each limb as a chain of points.

For wings, I'm adding an arm chain parented off the front leg's joint with thinner sweep radii and a darker green bone color, then attaching finger chains running from a wrist point to each tip, parented off the arm's end joint.

Now I'm setting up the thumb claw spike at the wrist and building the wing membrane by resampling between finger chains for thickness, defining the color palette with orange wing membrane, green body tones, cream/horn accents, and spike color.

I'm double-checking the foot and tail placements sit near the ground plane, then moving to write out the full export code while keeping imports clean and verifying parameter types for the spike helper function.
